notes: Step time = median of >= 5 uninstrumented steps (CUDA events) after warm-up; the traced captures are separate.
3 captures of 2 steps per variant; analyze() runs on each and the spread is reported.
Tracer overhead (~10-30 us host time per op) inflates launch-bound gaps; FLOPs/bytes per op are [MODELED].
Pageable vs pinned and the per-layer .item() are deliberate pathologies of the baseline step.

findings.evidence: 2 large copies from pageable memory, 32 MiB, 10.0 ms total at 3.4 GB/s (no pinned copy in this capture); host thread blocked and no kernel overlaps them
findings.recommendation: Pin the source buffers (DataLoader pin_memory=True or a pinned staging pool), copy with non_blocking=True on a side stream one step ahead, and make the compute stream wait on an event.

findings.evidence: 5 host-sync gaps per step, 1.34 ms GPU idle per step; the CPU blocks on .item()/synchronize and the GPU drains before new work arrives
findings.recommendation: Remove the per-layer debug .item() hook; accumulate metrics on the GPU and read them once every N steps; time steps with CUDA events instead of cudaDeviceSynchronize.

findings.evidence: 91 kernels/step shorter than 10 µs (median 4.1 µs, grid size not captured on a 24-SM GPU); 14 launch-bound gaps/step totalling 14.55 ms
findings.recommendation: Use fused/foreach optimizer kernels (multi-tensor apply), flatten small parameters into one buffer, or capture the optimizer step in a CUDA Graph.

findings.evidence: 13 gap(s)/step totalling 3.37 ms where the next kernel (aten::_to_copy) had been submitted long before the GPU went idle: the compute stream was waiting on an event from another stream
findings.recommendation: Find the cudaStreamWaitEvent/cudaLaunchHostFunc pair (here a monitoring callback) and take the host function off the compute stream's dependency chain (record an event and poll it later).
